headline: Carlmont's Homecoming Ran Loud Until 11 PM, and Neighbors Weren't Happy
story:
On Saturday, October 24, Carlmont High School held its annual Homecoming on the school field. The event ran until 11 PM with loud music and casino games, and by most accounts students had a great night.

The school's neighbors had a different night. Around 10 PM, people living nearby went on Nextdoor, the neighborhood social app, asking what the loud noise was. They traced it to Carlmont, and some pointed out that it was the weekend and they just wanted to get some rest.

They had reason to be frustrated. Belmont's noise ordinance treats weekend hours after 7 PM as nighttime, when the city sets stricter limits on noise near homes. Homecoming's music kept going four hours past that. It's unclear whether Carlmont had a permit or exemption to run that late.

The night also featured blackjack and roulette for students who are mostly under 18, California's minimum gambling age. Even when no real money changes hands, researchers have raised concerns about gambling-style games aimed at teens. A 2022 study of more than 1,600 Australian 12- to 17-year-olds found that teens who played simulated gambling games reported more signs of problem gambling. The study couldn't prove the games caused it, but it's reason enough to ask why they were part of the school's biggest fall event.

Carlmont's principal should address both issues. Tell neighbors and students whether the school had a permit for amplified music until 11 PM, and end future outdoor events at a time that respects the city's noise rules. And reconsider casino games at school events.

Carlmont can throw a great Homecoming without angering its neighbors or putting a blackjack table in front of freshmen.
